newsitem.title: UK: Thousands march through London to protest gun laws.
newsitem.headline: Thousands march through London to protest gun laws.

text.p: Around 10,000 gun enthusiasts marched through central London on Saturday to protest against plans to outlaw most firearms in response to a massacre of schoolchildren.
Representatives handed in a petition with 64,000 signatures to No 10 Downing Street, the official residence of Prime Minister John Major.

Britain already has some of the world's strictest gun legislation. Pressure for even stricter controls has been led by the bereaved parents of Dunblane, the Scottish town where lone gunman Thomas Hamilton gunned down 16 small children and their teacher last March before killing himself.
Saturday's marchers said ministers should concentrate instead on tighter vetting to prevent weapons falling into the wrong hands.
"This (draft legislation) will not work," Albie Fox, chairman of the newly-created Sportsmen's Association of Great Britain, told reporters. "It will not prevent another Dunblane."

Fox also promised to take a letter of thanks to the Duke of Edinburgh, who last month triggered a storm of criticism by criticising the government's plans and saying guns were no more dangerous than cricket bats.
The government introduced the new gun controls after the massacre but resisted the total ban on handguns sought by the murdered childrens' parents.
